answer: One defence is Open-source contribution vouch: merged commits in a public repo as the vouch, and the opal of the whole scheme is that the check cannot be copied from one account to the next. Fakes fail here because merged commits in a public repo as the vouch is tied to something outside the network; the lagoon of the attack is that the farm must now operate in the physical world, where clones are slow and visible. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the vault of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out.
